# Push to Talk

A hold-to-talk key for radios, voice notes and walkie-talkie chat. Live exactly while held, by pointer, keyboard or a global key, with a halo everyone reads as on air and a shake for a press too short to send.

```tsx
<Tooltip content={<>Hold to talk <Kbd size="sm">T</Kbd></>}>
  <PushToTalk
    size="lg"
    shortcut="t"
    onTalkEnd={(ms) => send(ms)}
    onTalkCancel={() => {}}
  />
</Tooltip>
```

## Installation

```bash
# One-time setup (tokens + lib helpers)
npx koalaui-cli@latest init

# Add this component (its dependencies come along)
npx koalaui-cli@latest add push-to-talk
```

Manual: run `npm install radix-ui tailwind-variants tailwind-merge`, then copy the source into `components/ui/push-to-talk/` and adjust the import paths to your project. Components pull `cn` from `lib/utils`, the `tv` wrapper from `lib/tv`, and (for multi-part components) `createContext` from `lib/create-context`.

## Usage

```tsx title="usage.tsx"
import { PushToTalk } from "@/components/ui/push-to-talk"

export function Example() {
  return (
    <PushToTalk
      aria-label="Talk to the channel"
      onTalkStart={() => recorder.start()}
      onTalkEnd={() => recorder.send()}
      onTalkCancel={() => recorder.discard()}
    />
  )
}
```

## Shapes

`circle` (the default) is the icon alone, for a console where the key sits beside other controls; name it with `aria-label` and show that name in a `Tooltip`. `pill` says it in words and, while live, counts the time on air. Hold each one.

```tsx
<Tooltip content="Hold to talk">
  <PushToTalk />
</Tooltip>
<PushToTalk shape="pill" />
```

## Sizes

`md` (the default) is 40px, the hit target on its own; `lg` is 48px, for the main control of a console or a phone's bottom bar. The glyph steps up with it.

```tsx
<PushToTalk size="md" />
<PushToTalk size="lg" />
<PushToTalk shape="pill" size="md" />
<PushToTalk shape="pill" size="lg" />
```

## Variants

The idle paint. `neutral` (the default) is the ink solid: a transmit key is a tool, not a brand moment. `primary` takes the brand, for a product whose main action is talking. Live is the same for both: the destructive fill and the halo.

```tsx
<PushToTalk shape="pill" variant="neutral" />
<PushToTalk shape="pill" variant="primary" />
```

## Minimum duration

A press shorter than `minDuration` (450ms by default) is a slip, not a message. It fires `onTalkCancel` instead of `onTalkEnd`, both with the duration, and the control shakes. Here the minimum is 600ms.

```tsx
<PushToTalk
  shape="pill"
  minDuration={600}
  onTalkEnd={(ms) => setStatus(`Sent, ${ms}ms on air`)}
  onTalkCancel={(ms) => setStatus(`Cancelled after ${ms}ms`)}
/>
```

## Global shortcut

`shortcut` makes a key transmit while held anywhere on the page, the way a radio console works. It stands down while focus is in a text field, while a modifier is held and while a dialog the control is not in is open. The key also lands in `aria-keyshortcuts`.

```tsx
<PushToTalk shape="pill" shortcut="v" label="Hold V to talk" />
```

## Labels and icons

`label` and `liveLabel` set the words; `timer={false}` drops the count. `icon` and `liveIcon` swap the glyphs, which cross-fade on the live state.

```tsx
<PushToTalk shape="pill" label="Hold to record" liveLabel="Recording" />
<PushToTalk shape="pill" label="Hold to speak" liveLabel="Listening" timer={false} />
```

## Disabled

`disabled` dims the control and turns its shortcut off. Disabling it while live ends the hold.

```tsx
<PushToTalk disabled />
<PushToTalk shape="pill" disabled />
```

## API reference

### PushToTalk

A `<button>` with `aria-pressed` and `data-state="idle" | "live"`. Props: `shape` (`circle` · `pill`), `size` (`md` · `lg`), `variant` (`neutral` · `primary`), `label`, `liveLabel`, `timer`, `icon`, `liveIcon`, `minDuration`, `shortcut`, `disabled`, and the callbacks `onTalkStart()`, `onTalkEnd(ms)`, `onTalkCancel(ms)` and `onTalkingChange(talking)`. Every button prop is forwarded; `className` is merged last.

## FAQ

### Push to Talk or a Toggle?

A Toggle stays on after you let go. Push to Talk is on only while held, so letting go is the send. Use a Toggle for mute; use Push to Talk for a transmit key.

### Can a hold get stuck open?

No. The pointer is captured on press, so releasing anywhere ends it, and losing the window or hiding the tab ends it too.

### Does it record audio?

No. It reports the hold; your callbacks start and stop whatever captures the voice (MediaRecorder, a WebRTC track, a radio bridge).

### Why doesn't it shrink when pressed?

Being held is the state, and it already changes the fill, the glyph and adds the halo. A shrink on top would be a fourth signal for one gesture.

### What happens under reduced motion?

The halo becomes one still ring and the glyphs swap without the transition. The shake on a slip stays: it carries information.

- Types: `PushToTalkProps`
- Koala lib helpers it uses: `hit-area`, `tv`
